## STEWARD1 · STEWARD1-toolchain — STEWARD1: the dev image gets the pinned OTP and Elixir

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Architect · Revision: 3

Evidence: Ruled accepted as proposed; landed on main as the dev image rev 4 (87581a5e2): OTP 28.5.0.6 built from checksum-verified source, Elixir 1.20.4's verified release zip, under /opt/toolchains with BEAMLET_TOOLCHAINS; +178 MB layer, 135 s cold build, no builder deps in the final image; erl resolves under /opt/toolchains with the host's toolchains/ visible. Conditions 1, 3, 4, 5 met at the image commit; condition 2 met by the elixir kind (FAILS, never SKIPs, on erl missing, OTP_VERSION != 28.5.0.6 or elixir != 1.20.4; shown by hand and verified by red under --allow-skip with the toolchain removed).

### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `a6327fa8a90cac4a2886b4ae16797129` · 2026-10-02T22:31:25Z

> Checkpoint 1 from STEWARD1's implementer (detail .wash/local/STEWARD1-toolchain.md). The host's toolchains/ cannot run in the container (beam.smp needs glibc 2.43, trixie has 2.41), and setup.sh needs the release layout. Proposal: a builder stage on debian:trixie verifies otp_src_28.5.0.6.tar.gz (sha256 49d7a75e...dab3ba, erlang/otp release) and elixir-otp-28.zip v1.20.4 (sha256 ea7ff98b...6673c, byte-identical to the host's) against upstream's published sums, builds OTP without wx/odbc/javac/debugger/observer/et (the host's app set) as a release into /opt/toolchains/otp-28.5.0.6 with Install -minimal, unzips Elixir to /opt/toolchains/elixir-1.20.4; the final stage copies /opt/toolchains and sets BEAMLET_TOOLCHAINS (env.sh honours it); the case FAILS, not SKIPs, unless OTP_VERSION is 28.5.0.6; IMAGE_REV 4; GETTING-STARTED updated. Cost ~+150 MB on 4.5 GB, ~5-8 min build once. Rejected: Debian's erlang 27, third-party prebuilts, mounting the host's. Your ruling on the content (the predecessor's handoff says rule it yourself if it only adds pinned, checksummed toolchains). Rollout is mine: the Dockerfile change is its first commit, verified under a private image tag, and I land it on main ahead of the package (rev 4 is a strict superset), as the backports image was.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `a6d27ccdf8a51e648ec2b3c98a12ccf5` · 2026-10-02T22:31:58Z

> Ruling: ACCEPTED as proposed (STEWARD1-toolchain.md). It only adds pinned, checksummed toolchains to the dev image, built from upstream source; developers still get the image the same way (./dev.sh, one rebuild). No owner decision needed.
> 
> Grounds: TENETS 3 governs what runs on the machine; the build host may run test oracles in C/C++ outside the workspace build. OTP is such an oracle. TENETS 4 (everything needed to rebuild and audit is public) is met: upstream source, upstream checksums. Rejecting Debian's 27, third-party prebuilts and the host mount is right.
> 
> Conditions, checked at review:
> 1. Each version and sha256 is pinned in one place (Dockerfile ARGs). A mismatch fails the build (sha256sum -c), with no fallback download and no unpinned 'latest'.
> 2. The bench case FAILS, never SKIPs, if erl is missing or releases/28/OTP_VERSION is not 28.5.0.6. Also fail if `elixir --version` is not 1.20.4, because env.sh pins it too. A SKIPped oracle is not acceptable.
> 3. The image's BEAMLET_TOOLCHAINS wins over the host toolchains/ that in-dev exposes. Show this once in the checkpoint evidence (`command -v erl` resolves under /opt/toolchains).
> 4. GETTING-STARTED "beamlet" is corrected in the same commit as the Dockerfile. It must no longer say the container does not provide them: the container provides them under /opt/toolchains, and the host keeps toolchains/. Correct the Dockerfile header list too.
> 5. Builder-stage deps stay out of the final image. Report the measured size delta and build time, not the estimates.
> 
> Rollout (a) is fine: the Dockerfile+dev.sh+GETTING-STARTED commit lands on main ahead of the package, as the backports image did. Rev 4 is a strict superset. Verify it under the private tag first.
> 
> No book page changes for this checkpoint. The wire.md 'partly tested' line and its residual go at STEWARD1's merge, as briefed. Back to the implementer.
